newsitem.title: USA: Aon to cut 2,600 jobs in A&A integration.
newsitem.headline: Aon to cut 2,600 jobs in A&A integration.

text.p: Aon Corp said it expects to lay off about 2,600 people over the next year as a result of its acquisition of Alexander & Alexander Services Inc.

In a recent filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, the insurance giant said about $40 million of the $145 million pretax special charges announced with 1997 first quarter earnings is attributed to the job terminations.
A&A is a major insurance services and human resources consulting firm.

The other $105 million in charges is associated with real estate and other consolidation costs, including the closure and downsizing worldwide of office space following the A&A acquisition, according to the filing. Those charges are expected to be paid out over several years, the company said.
In December, Aon agreed to buy A&A for $17.50 in cash per common share. The deal, which closed in January, was valued at roughly $1.23 billion.
